scope: Proposition 2.1 (Deterministic reduction) of the manuscript “Balanced counterexamples to Ryser's conjecture at prime orders” (preprints/Balanced-Counterexamples-to-Rysers-Conjecture-at-Prime-Orders-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 162 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5be7cf2d1f382e80), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let q ≥ 4 be a prime power. Suppose a compatible collection of valid tuples in F2 q satisfies occupancy, concentration of core covers, and the local condition with parameters 0 < ρ < 1 and B ≥ 0. If ρq > 2(1 + B), (6) then there is an intersecting (q + 1)-partite (q + 1)-uniform hypergraph with exactly q + 1 nonisolated vertices in each part and cover number q + 1. Its edges are in bijection with the set X in (3).
